ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \angle DAC = 2x$, $ \angle ACB = 4x$, $ \angle ABC = 3x$, and $AD = BC$, then what is the value of $ \angle BAD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend BC to point E such that CE=BD,\\
$\therefore$BD+CD=CE+CD,\\
$\therefore$BC=DE,\\
$\because$AD=BC,\\
$\therefore$AD=DE,\\
$\therefore \angle E=\angle DAE$,\\
$\because \angle ACD=4x$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAE+\angle E=4x$,\\
$\therefore \angle E=4x-\angle CAE=\angle DAE$,\\
$\therefore 4x-\angle CAE =2x+\angle CAE$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAE =x$, $\angle DAE =\angle E =3x$,\\
$\because \angle ABC =3x$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC =\angle E$,\\
$\therefore AB=AE$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABD \cong \triangle AEC$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADB=\angle ACE$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADC=\angle ACD=4x$,\\
$\because \angle ADC+\angle ACD+\angle DAC =180^\circ$,\\
$\therefore 4x+4x+2x=180^\circ$,\\
Solving for: $x=18^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAD= \boxed{18^\circ}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $\angle DAC = 2x$, $\angle ACB = 4x$, $\angle ABC = 3x$, and $AD = BC$. What is the value of $\angle BAD$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $BC$ to point $E$ such that $CE = BD$,\\
$\therefore BD + CD = CE + CD$,\\
$\therefore BC = DE$,\\
$\because AD = BC$,\\
$\therefore AD = DE$,\\
$\therefore \angle E = \angle DAE$,\\
$\because \angle ACD = 4x$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAE + \angle E = 4x$,\\
$\therefore \angle E = 4x - \angle CAE = \angle DAE$,\\
$\therefore 4x - \angle CAE = 2x + \angle CAE$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAE = x$, $\angle DAE = \angle E = 3x$,\\
$\because \angle ABC = 3x$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC = \angle E$,\\
$\therefore AB = AE$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABD \cong \triangle AEC$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADB = \angle ACE$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADC = \angle ACD = 4x$,\\
$\because \angle ADC + \angle ACD + \angle DAC = 180^\circ$,\\
$\therefore 4x + 4x + 2x = 180^\circ$,\\
Solving for: $x = 18^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAD = \boxed{18^\circ}$
